aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:856.description: For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer. Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations. If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer! A Brief Overview Portland’s newest venue is a 68,000-square-foot facility designed to support dynamic, large-scale live events. It offers flexible seating for 2,000 to 4,250 attendees and features a movable stage that enables multiple event configurations, making it well suited for the city’s diverse live music scene. Located at the former Nordstrom site on NE Multnomah Street, the venue sits within the Lloyd District and the Lloyd Entertainment District—an area known for its creative energy and accessibility. The venue also provides convenient access to light rail and streetcar lines, as well as a north–south bike and pedestrian bridge. Extensive surface and adjacent parking is available at nearby Lloyd Mall structures, reflecting Portland’s emphasis on connectivity, community, and vibrant urban experiences. The General Manager is responsible for the overall management and operation of the facility, including staffing, finance, marketing, production, maintenance, and related functions, while ensuring compliance with all federal and local safety regulations. This role provides organizational leadership and serves as a liaison between corporate staff, vendors, and venue partners. Establish and manage the annual operating calendar, including initial programming strategy, hours of operation, and attendance and revenue projections for venue launch and ongoing operations. Develop, implement, and monitor operating budgets; oversee cost control and financial performance for operations and events. Identify and pursue partnership opportunities to enhance revenue, operations, and community presence. Develop and execute community engagement strategies; represent the organization at public events and build relationships with local stakeholders. flagshippioneeringinc-flagshippioneering.description: Position Summary: Prologue Medicines are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Senior RA to join our dynamic In Vivo Biology team, leading projects in discovery and pre-clinical development for therapeutic proteins of viral origin. The successful candidate will play a key role in designing, executing, and analyzing in vivo studies to evaluate therapeutic proteins with the aim of nominating development candidates, and supporting preclinical development and translational science of these molecules through to IND and beyond. As a member of our team, you will be responsible for designing and executing experiments to understand the activity, mechanism of action, and therapeutic potential of early-stage biologics in vivo . This role offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment, working independently as well as collaboratively within a highly integrated team. This is an on-site role in Somerville, MA. Key Responsibilities: Planning, execution, and analysis of in vivo experiments to evaluate the therapeutic potential of our test articles including pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic, biodistribution, and efficacy studies. Conducting ex vivo wet lab experiments to analyze PD phenotypes and MoA in different tissues. Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team to design, plan and execute experiments, and manage outcomes to support research activities, project goals, and platform development. Creative and strategic contributions to the discussions, designs, and implementation of in vivo and ex vivo Managing relationships with external research facilities. Reporting results to the scientific team and management. Critical data analysis, attention to detail, and troubleshooting abilities. Maintaining an organized and up-to-date electronic lab notebook. Writing, updating, and maintain high-quality experimental protocols. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s or MS degree with 3+ years of relevant experience with in vivo and ex vivo lab experiments in accademia or industry. Extensive experience with mouse handling: injections (IV, IM, IP), blood collection, and tissue harvesting is essential. Performing and recording animal health observations, communicating adverse findings to the veterinarian technicians to ensure animal care standards are in keeping with applicable laws and regulatory guidelines. Writes and maintains animal protocols. Experienced with various ELN and LIMS systems. Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of conveying technical information in a clear and thorough manner, document results in laboratory notebooks. Demonstrated ability to work in a highly collaborative team environment. Motivated and excited about biological discovery and assay development. A dynamic problem solver and self-starter Preferred Requirements: Hands on experience in a variety of ex vivo / in vitro analysis techniques such as ELISA, MSD, Luminex, ELISpot, and flow cytometry from a wide range of different tissue types. A proven track record of developing and optimizing disease efficacy models in mice. Flagship Pioneering and our ecosystem companies are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. At Flagship, we recognize there is no perfect candidate. If you have some of the experience listed above but not all, please apply anyway. Experience comes in many forms, skills are transferable, and passion goes a long way. We are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams and look forward to learning more about your unique background. ryzlabs-ryzlabs:lever:c02024b7-98b2-4170.description: RYZ Labs is looking for a Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer to join one of our client’s teams, a performance advertising company! You'll ship features into a live PHP monolith that runs a performance advertising business, and you'll help design the services they break out of it. The work starts in the monolith, because that's where the business runs today — and the decisions you make there are what the next architecture gets built on. Basic Qualifications: • 7+ years building and operating production web applications • Deep PHP experience in a long-lived, server-rendered application you were responsible for • You've shipped and operated an integration against a major ad platform's API — Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, or Google/YouTube. We mean the real thing: rate limits and backoff, token rotation, async report jobs, version deprecations, backfilling after an outage • You can talk credibly about normalizing data across more than one ad platform — where the object models refuse to line up, why the same campaign reports different numbers in two places, and how you decide which one billing gets to believe • Strong vanilla JavaScript, and comfort in a modern component framework — you'll be introducing one, not inheriting one • You've owned a system where a bad change costs real money, and you can talk about blast radius, rollback, and how you verify a data change before you run it • Self-directed across time zones, and clear in writing What makes you stand out: • Production Go • Background job and queue systems — retries, idempotency, work that survives a reboot • An understanding of how commercial media-buying automation platforms are built. You don't need to have built one. We want someone who can reason about how those systems work and what's worth building versus buying • Dense operational UI — data grids, bulk actions, review queues, spreadsheet export. This is what our ad ops team stares at all day • Docker and twelve-factor instincts • Shipping AI-backed features, not just using AI to write code — evaluating model output, precision versus recall, and what a false positive costs when a human is downstream Key Responsibilities: Ad Platform Integration: This is the heart of the role. They are deep in the Meta Marketing API — campaign and creative objects, insights and spend, audience exclusions, duplicate-ad detection, and the policy surfaces that tell them when an ad is in trouble — and they are bringing TikTok, Snapchat, and YouTube online now. Four platforms means four object models, four sets of rate limits, four ideas of what a conversion window is, and one internal model that has to make sense of all of them. Designing that abstraction well is the highest-leverage thing anyone there can do this year. Compliance and Creative Review: The products their ad ops team runs on: AI-assisted creative checking, rescanning live ads for compliance drift, flagging unsubstantiated claims and unlicensed likeness or music, and the human review queues wrapped around all of it. Revenue Systems: Billing rules, referral commission logic based on advertiser spend, and reconciling what the platforms report against what they recorded. Spend numbers move after the fact. If you already know why that matters for billing, we should talk. Making Shipping Safe: Meet their new deployment pipeline halfway from the application side: a migration system so no schema change reaches production by hand, tests where a bug costs them money, and making the app stateless so they can eventually run more than one of it.
